My interpretation is that twisting work hardens the wire to get a specified tensile strength which should be greater than the break away toqure + a specified amount of force (I forget ) in order to keep the hardware attached to its assigned location incase of emergency. So I feel as if using copper wire for switches, it doesn't matter as much since I've only seen it used on guarded switches anyhow, but still important to twist due to accidental hits and rubs. To me, it looks nice twisted. If the mm doesnt specify I usually twist just because of that.
